title: 2015 AMC 8 Problem 11
statement: In the small country of Mathland, all automobile license plates have four symbols. The first must be a vowel (A, E, I, O, or U), the second and third must be two different letters among the \(21\) non-vowels, and the fourth must be a digit (0 through \(9\)). If the symbols are chosen at random subject to these conditions, what is the probability that the plate will read “AMC8”?

solutions.text:
There are \(5\) choices for the first symbol, \(21\) choices for the second, \(20\) choices for the third because it must be a different non-vowel, and \(10\) choices for the final digit.

Thus there are \(5\cdot21\cdot20\cdot10=21{,}000\) possible plates. Exactly one of these is AMC8, so the probability is \(\dfrac{1}{21{,}000}.\)

Thus, B is the correct answer.
hints: Count all license plates allowed by the rules.
Only one of those plates is exactly AMC8.
